title: Hourglass of Time
next_chapter_hook: The thirty-day countdown has begun. When Chen Ji finally found that crack in Heavenly Secrets, what awaited him was not the expected flaw—but a pair of eyes that had never closed.

text.content:
The speed at which the cracks spread exceeded everyone's expectations.

Chen Ji stood at the Cliff of the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain, watching the black fissure connecting heaven and earth devour the sky at a visible rate. The once clear heavens were now like torn silk, revealing the chaotic Void behind it. Wind poured from the crack, carrying the scent of decay and ending.

"Every prophecy is a nail," Mo Xiansheng's voice drifted from the Void. "The more you drive in, the more unstable this heaven becomes."

Chen Ji did not answer. His fingertips trembled slightly—not from fear, but because of that number. When he had glimpsed the future again moments ago, the predicted time had plummeted from three hours to less than one. The consumption of Heavenly Fate Value remained unchanged, but the range he could perceive was contracting rapidly.

"Time is collapsing," Mo Xiansheng's voice carried a rare weight. "Every time you rewrite fate, you chisel a hole in the timeline of this realm. Now those holes are connecting."

The sea of clouds below the Cliff began to boil, as if something was awakening from the depths. Chen Ji drew a deep breath, pressing his inner turmoil into the depths of his dantian. Panic solves nothing—this was the most profound lesson he had learned through years of cultivation.

dialogue.content:
"What are you calculating?"

Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul coalesced beside Chen Ji, his perpetually blurred features now showing a hint of worry.

"Calculating how much time I have left." Chen Ji's voice was terrifyingly calm. "Each use of the Tianji Record consumes 5 points of Heavenly Fate Value. I currently have approximately three hundred points remaining. In other words, I can still glimpse the future sixty more times, rewrite fate sixty more times."

He raised his head, his gaze piercing through the countless cracks in the sky: "Sixty chances. Is that enough to set up a guaranteed victory?"

Mo Xiansheng was silent for a moment: "Your calculations are not wrong. But you overlooked one thing."

"What?"

"The timeline is fracturing." Mo Xiansheng's voice was low. "Every timeline you have altered leaves a wound. Those wounds will not heal—they will only multiply and deepen. When they become numerous enough—"

He did not finish, but Chen Ji already understood.

When the wounds became numerous enough, this heaven and earth itself would shatter. Then别说改写命运 he wouldn't even have room to survive.

text.content:
Chen Ji closed his eyes.

He thought of those fates he had rewritten—during the Inner Sect Tournament when Han Lie's meridians suddenly reversed flow, forcing him to concede; before the Demonic Path's army pressed in, seven core generals simultaneously went into qi deviation; Ling Yuan's years-long power-grabbing scheme, collapsing due to a sudden internal rebellion.

Each time was precise, covert cost transfer. He never acted directly, only pried at fate's fulcrum, making the impossible happen. Back then he thought he had mastered everything.

Now he understood: fate is never meant to be mastered.

It is a net, and any struggle only makes it wrap tighter. And every "rewrite" he made over these years was just cutting more holes in this net. When the holes were numerous enough, the entire net would fall apart.

"So this is the price." Chen Ji said softly. "Not retribution, not divine punishment, but the simplest—dominoes. I knocked over the first piece, and now the entire world awaits collapse."

Mo Xiansheng did not deny it.

dialogue.content:
At that moment, a sound beyond words echoed from the depths of the heavens.

The sound was indescribable—it did not come from any direction, but rang directly in Chen Ji's consciousness, as if heaven and earth themselves were speaking. Every syllable carried irresistible authority, as if the world's laws of operation were making way for it.

"Chen Ji."

Only two words, yet they sent a shudder through the depths of Chen Ji's soul. It was a feeling he had never experienced—more intense than facing Ling Yuan, more intense than facing the Demonic Path's Saint. This was not the pressure of some powerful being, but something transcendent examining him.

"You have seen."

The voice continued, carrying a calm近乎怜悯: "Countless have tried to glimpse fate's reverse side. They thought they found flaws, thought they could jump out of the chessboard."

"But you are not the first."

Chen Ji猛地抬头，声音艰涩: "Who are you?"

"I am what you have always been opposing." The voice answered. "And what you have always been part of without realizing. I have no name, but if I must be called—"

"You may call me, the Eye of Heavenly Secrets."

text.content:
The Eye of Heavenly Secrets.

Chen Ji had heard this title in Mo Xiansheng's scattered words, but never truly understood its meaning. Now, facing this voice directly, he finally understood.

This was not merely a title. This was heaven's own will, the core law of fate's operation, the most original "cause" of this heaven and earth.

All prophecy, divination, and Heavenly Secrets techniques were nothing but secretions of this Eye. And the Tianji Record in his hands was merely a small fragment broken off from this Eye.

He had been using his fragment to oppose the entire Heavenly Secrets.

"You always knew." Chen Ji spoke with difficulty, his voice even more hoarse than before: "You knew the Tianji Record was in my hands, knew I was using it to rewrite fate, knew of Ling Yuan's schemes, Han Lie's ambition, Ye Qing's identity—you knew everything."

"Of course." The Eye of Heavenly Secrets' voice was terrifyingly calm: "What you call "variables" are merely predetermined paths within this chess game. I allowed you to change some pieces, because those changes themselves are part of my plan."

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji's fist slowly tightened within his sleeve.

He did not like this feeling. Not anger, not fear, but something deeper, a厌恶发自骨髓.

He recalled his days being bullied in the Sect's Servants' Quarters as a child. Those people had said the same thing—"Everything you have is given by us, without the Sect you are nothing." Back then he chose to endure, chose to hone his claws in silence.

Until one day, those people's fates were gently nudged by him.

Now, someone else stood in the same position telling him: "Your struggle is also something I permit."

"If that were truly the case," Chen Ji raised his head, his lips actually forming a smile: "Then why have you appeared in person?"

The Eye of Heavenly Secrets fell silent for a moment.

"Because your existence has begun to make me feel... displeasure."

This sentence made Chen Ji's heart jolt. Displeasure. This meant he had done something right. This meant his existence truly touched a nerve of Heavenly Secrets.

"Therefore," the Eye of Heavenly Secrets' voice sounded again, this time carrying a hint of judgment: "It is time to reclaim this fragment."

text.content:
At that moment, Mo Xiansheng's voice sounded in Chen Ji's mind, audible only to him:

"It has given you a thirty-day deadline."

Chen Ji froze. The Eye of Heavenly Secrets' words had been authoritative, but had mentioned no specific time limit.

"Outside your perception, it has already transmitted the information to you." Mo Xiansheng's voice was urgent: "This is Heavenly Secrets' law—it will not directly destroy any existence, even an ant. It gives the target a chance to catch its breath, then watches as the other walks toward destruction in hope. After thirty days, if you have not made a choice—"

"What choice?"

"Accept its arrangement, become a true chess piece. Or—" Mo Xiansheng paused: "Proactively sacrifice the Tianji Record, in exchange for the safety of those you cherish."

Chen Ji was silent.

He lowered his gaze to his own hands, those hands that had countless times nudged the threads of fate. Slender joints, ordinary lines—they looked no different from any Servant Disciple's hands.

But these very hands had clawed out from among the dead, reversed impossible situations from the brink of despair, transformed from atrash everyone dismissed into an existence that made the three great Sects lose sleep.

Now, they faced an ultimate test.

dialogue.content:
"What do you intend to do?"

Mo Xiansheng's voice pulled Chen Ji back from contemplation. His remnant soul floated in the air, features still blurred, but his eyes seemed to hold a hint of expectation.

"I have one question." Chen Ji did not answer directly, but asked: "Where did the Tianji Record originally come from?"

Mo Xiansheng fell into a long silence.

"...This question, I should not answer."

"But you did not say 'cannot.'" Chen Ji stared at the vague soul mass: "You hesitated. This means the answer favors me."

Mo Xiansheng let out a sigh-like laugh: "You are always like this, skilled at finding the finest crack in the most desperate circumstances."

"Then tell me."

"The Tianji Record," Mo Xiansheng's voice dropped low: "is a piece of rotting flesh carved from this Eye of Heavenly Secrets."

Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply.

"What do you mean?"

"Heavenly Secrets is not eternally unchanging." Mo Xiansheng revealed a truth he had never disclosed: "In an incomprehensibly distant past, this Heavenly Secrets once... rotted. It produced things it could not digest, so it stripped those things away, abandoning them in the mortal realm."

"The Tianji Record is one of those abandoned things. It does not belong to Heavenly Secrets—it was once Heavenly Secrets' lesion."

text.content:
This truth was like a thunderclap, exploding in Chen Ji's consciousness.

He had always believed the Tianji Record was some supreme treasure surpassing Heavenly Secrets, his greatest reliance for surviving in this world. Now he learned that this thing was from the beginning Heavenly Secrets' castoff, a hidden danger it was eager to be rid of.

He thought he was grasping a weapon against heaven, but it was merely a piece of discarded rotting flesh.

But strangely, this discovery did not make him feel dejected.

恰恰相反, when Chen Ji raised his head again, his eyes blazed with a flame he had never possessed before.

"So the Eye of Heavenly Secrets wants to recover the Tianji Record from my hands, not because I threaten it." He spoke slowly, his voice carrying an icy certainty: "But because what I hold is something it once desperately tried to cast off."

Mo Xiansheng did not speak, but his silence itself was affirmation.

"What it fears is not me." Chen Ji laughed—this time a real, heartfelt smile: "It fears what will happen when this rotting flesh grows back onto it."

dialogue.content:
Thirty days.

Chen Ji recited this number in his heart. He did not know if he still had thirty days—the Eye of Heavenly Secrets mentioned a final deadline, but not an execution date. Who knew if it would strike early, if it would end everything before he was ready.

But he had to gamble.

He thought of Su Qingyao. The unhealing crack still remained on her body, and every use of the Tianji Record widened that crack further. If he continued, she would bear more backlash for him, until—

He dared not think further.

He thought of Chen Nian. His younger sister, taken by the Holy Sect as a "Heavenly Fate Lock Key." Her existence interfered with the Tianji Record's foresight, making any scene containing her grow blurry. She was his only weakness, and his only exception.

If he fell, who would save her?

"You are thinking of them." Mo Xiansheng's voice carried no emotional color: "This will interfere with your judgment."

"No." Chen Ji shook his head: "This will make me clearer."

He drew a deep breath, beginning to calculate every move ahead in his heart. Thirty days, he had much to do. First, he must understand the Eye of Heavenly Secrets' true weakness. Second, he must prepare Su Qingyao and Ye Qing for the worst. Finally, he must find Chen Nian—wherever she was, whatever the cost.

"Time is running out." He said softly.

"It never is." Mo Xiansheng replied: "For anyone attempting to defy heaven and change fate, time has always been the most奢侈的东西."

The cost was 5 points of Heavenly Fate Value, and the increasingly frequent timeline collapses that followed. But he had no choice.

Mo Xiansheng did not stop him. They both understood, some costs must be paid.

"Chen Nian..." He silently recited his sister's name, the light at his fingertips growing brighter.

Blurry images began forming before his eyes—a place he had never seen, filled with the气息 of decay and death. And in the depths of that气息, a figure with features similar to his own slowly turned its head.

text.content:
"Mo Xiansheng." Chen Ji spoke, his voice surprisingly calm: "Since the Tianji Record is Heavenly Secrets' rotting flesh, what exactly happened before it was stripped away?"

Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul shuddered slightly. This question touched upon some extremely ancient taboo.

"...This question, I originally should not answer."

"But you did not say 'cannot.'" Chen Ji repeated his earlier words: "You hesitated. Hesitation means the answer favors me."

Silence.

Mountain wind howling past, stirring Mo Xiansheng's ethereal robes. After a long while, he spoke: "Long, long ago, the Eye of Heavenly Secrets attempted a new mode of operation. It wanted to completely fix fate, to have every living being run on preset tracks, allowing no deviation."

"And the result?"

"The result was that it produced obsession it could not itself digest. Those obsessions accumulated more and more, ultimately becoming... rotting flesh." Mo Xiansheng's voice became ethereal: "And the Tianji Record is the crystallization of those obsessions."

text.content:
Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes.

He pressed his palm against the cover of the Tianji Record, feeling that familiar power surge through his fingertips. This was his greatest reliance, his foundation for surviving in this world. Without it, he would be that humiliatedtrash servant, that卑微existence who could never hold his head high.

But at the same time, he thought of the cracks on Su Qingyao.

Every time he used the Tianji Record, those cracks would spread a little further. She said nothing, but he could clearly see the pain in her eyes. She was bearing the cost for him, yet never asked for anything in return.

"Enough." he said softly, his voice carrying a tenderness that even surprised himself, "Let's pause for now."

The light of the Tianji Record dimmed in his palm. A sense of emptiness rushed in, as if something had been extracted from his body.

But his heart was more peaceful than it had ever been.

No matter which path is chosen, the ending will come.

Chen Ji raised his head, looking at the sky that was collapsing above him. The cracks had already spread to near his head, and chaotic void seeped through from the fissures, like some formless beast gnawing at the edges of this world.

He suddenly remembered a story from his childhood. It was about a fisherman who pulled an old divine lamp from the bottom of the sea. After wiping it clean, the lamp spirit appeared and promised to grant him three wishes.

The fisherman was overjoyed, but cautious. He spent an entire day contemplating his wishes, ensuring each one was flawless.

But just as he was about to speak, a storm rose on the sea. A giant wave struck, and both fisherman and lamp sank to the bottom of the sea together.

At the story's end, the storyteller asked him: "What wisdom does this story teach us?"

He couldn't answer at the time.

Now he understood.

The wisdom was: fate does not wait for you to be ready. It descends when you are least prepared, teaching you in the cruelest way what "helplessness" truly means.

But at the same time, fate never truly abandons anyone. As long as one still lives, there remains a chance for a comeback.

He, Chen Ji, has never been someone who accepts fate.

"Thirty days."

Chen Ji repeated this number in his heart, then turned and walked toward the mountain's base.

He did not know what would happen in these thirty days, did not know if the Eye of Heavenly Dao would strike first, did not know if those envious enemies would take advantage of the crisis. He did not even know if the path he had chosen could even be walked.

But there was one thing he was certain of.

No matter whether the road ahead was smooth or a precipice, he would walk it step by step. Not because of confidence, but because there was no retreat.

Behind him, the remnant soul of Mo Xiansheng watched his departing figure and let out a meaningful sigh.

"The chess game has entered its final phase." he murmured to himself, "And the outcome of this game will determine the fate of the entire world."

The cracks in the sky expanded once more.

The thirty-day countdown thus began.
